mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT mobility has improved from -30.0 to -27.3 percent change over four weeks, and this transit recovery signals broader reopening of movement that raises discretionary retail footfall, producing higher RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than or equal to its last 28-day mean while TRANSIT continues to improve over the same four-week window.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL has fallen from 6.6 to 3.7 percent change over four weeks, indicating people spend less time at home and more time in out-of-home activities, which lifts RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL continues declining but RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is not higher than its last 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both recover concurrently, with WORKPLACES rising from -9.7 to -8.4 and TRANSIT from -30.0 to -27.3; the joint return of commuting and transit use multiplies retail-and-recreation trips, driving RETAIL_REC upward over four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both rise week-on-week for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: When WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both rise for two consecutive weeks, RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is not higher than its last 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: A TRANSIT crossing above -28.0 percent change marks a policy-driven relaxation of mobility constraints; once this threshold is crossed, retail and recreation mobility follows transit recovery upward over two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises above -28.0 percent change week-on-week
failure_condition: After TRANSIT crosses above -28.0, RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days fails to exceed its prior 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS dropped sharply to -27.3 then rebounded to -16.9, a swing that signals a seasonal turn toward outdoor activity; this outdoor seasonality spills over into retail-and-recreation spending within one week.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises by more than 8 points week-on-week after falling below -25.0
failure_condition: PARKS rebounds more than 8 points after a sub -25.0 reading, but RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is not higher than its last 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM declines from 2.3 to 1.3 while TRANSIT recovers from -30.0 to -27.3, indicating a shift from necessity grocery trips to discretionary retail trips; the substitution plus transit recovery raises RETAIL_REC over two weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM falls below 1.5 and TRANSIT rises above -29.0
failure_condition: If GROCERY_PHARM is below 1.5 and TRANSIT above -29.0, RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than or equal to its last 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: In a tightening-restrictions regime, a WORKPLACES drop below -10.0 percent change signals renewed closures that suppress retail-and-recreation activity, pushing RETAIL_REC lower over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES falls below -10.0 percent change week-on-week
failure_condition: After WORKPLACES falls below -10.0, RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is higher than or equal to its last 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC itself has improved from -8.0 to -7.0 over four weeks, and a crossing above -7.5 signals positive momentum that attracts further retail-and-recreation visits over the next week, lifting the four-week mean.
candidate_trigger: RETAIL_REC rises above -7.5 percent change week-on-week
failure_condition: After RETAIL_REC crosses above -7.5, the next 28-day mean of RETAIL_REC is not higher than its last 28-day mean.
